behavior.pattern: A row of togglable buttons where one (single mode) or several (multiple mode) may be pressed at once — the button-based cousin of radio-group's input-based single-selection pattern, per the general APG toolbar/radiogroup conventions the linked Radix docs cite. THE HEADLINE STRUCTURAL QUESTION THIS MATRIX HAD TO ANSWER FIRST: is single-vs-multiple a real, first-class axis in all three systems, or does one system only pretend to have it? Answer, confirmed by reading the real source rather than assuming from the `Value` type alias: shadcn's `type: "single" | "multiple"` is a real, first-class Radix prop, demonstrated live in both `toggle-group-demo.tsx` (type="multiple") and `toggle-group-single.tsx` (type="single") [S]. M3's `SegmentedButtonSet.multiselect: boolean` is real, sourced, live JS logic — `setButtonSelected()` branches on it directly, deselecting every sibling in single mode, leaving siblings untouched in multi mode [S]. Salt's `ToggleButtonGroup`, despite its own `Value` type permitting `string | readonly string[] | number | undefined`, is CONFIRMED SINGLE-SELECT-ONLY: `role="radiogroup"` is a HARDCODED literal (not conditional on any prop), `isSelected(id) { return value === id }` uses strict equality against ONE held value (an array value would only ever match by reference, never by content, so multi-select is a TYPE ARTIFACT, not a working capability), and no `ToggleButtonGroupProps` field of any kind selects a selection mode [S, confirmed absence of a working multi-select path despite the permissive type]. A second real structural finding: M3 uses exactly ONE aria pattern — `role="group"` on the set, `aria-pressed` on every button — for BOTH single AND multi-select modes, never switching to `role="radiogroup"`/`role="radio"` the way shadcn's Radix implementation is presumed to for `type="single"` [S, confirmed by reading segmented-button-set.ts/segmented-button.ts in full — no role branching on `multiselect` exists anywhere].
behavior.chassis: skeleton/toggle-group.tsx — written from the template's part union: a ToggleGroup wrapper (a <div> for Salt/shadcn, a <span> for M3, per structure.group's config strategy) providing context to any number of ToggleGroupItem children, each a real native <button> (matching all three real sources — the first component in this pipeline where NO column needed a declared native-element APPROXIMATION at the item level; every real source already renders a genuine <button>). Selection state: value may be a single string (single mode) or a string array (multiple mode), matching shadcn's real, richer API shape — the ONE internal engine this chassis implements for all three columns, a declared simplification for Salt (whose real source only ever drives the single-string path) and a declared simplification for M3 (whose real source drives a per-item boolean rather than a shared array, converging on the identical OBSERVABLE outcome). A SECOND declared choice, sourced directly rather than assumed: clicking an ALREADY-selected item in single mode DESELECTS it (value becomes undefined) — the presumed real Radix behaviour [R], and a genuine, sourced DIVERGENCE from Salt's own real ToggleButtonGroup, whose `select()` callback re-sets the SAME value on a repeat click and therefore never fires `onChange` and never deselects (grepped directly: `if (value !== newValue) { onChange?.(event) }` — an equal-value click is a silent no-op) — recorded here and in the matrix doc's findings rather than silently reproducing Salt's more restrictive behaviour as if it were universal. Every item is a REAL, unconditionally rendered <button> (no ref-reading effect on a conditionally-mounted node anywhere in this file — the same dialog-trap-immune shape checkbox.tsx/switch.tsx/radio-group.tsx already have). Icon content is wrapped in its own [data-slot="toggle-group-item-icon"] span, explicitly sized (CLAUDE.md rule 12 — see structure.icon-slot), matching the exact fix POPOVER-MATRIX.md findings 9/10 record for an unconstrained SVG.
